# The village economy, as built

The source of truth for how tokens are created, held, moved and destroyed in
Village OS. Every claim here is measured against the code or against the live
Amora database. Where the code and the intention differ, this file says so rather
than describing the intention.

**Two companion files.** `docs/TOKENS.md` is GENERATED by
`scripts/generate-token-doc.mjs` and guarded by `scripts/check-token-doc.mjs`, so
it cannot drift: it is the registry, the rules and the amounts, and it is the
machine-checkable half. This file is the narrative around it, written by hand,
and it can drift. When they disagree, `docs/TOKENS.md` is right.

Measured against production 2026-09-03 unless stated otherwise.

---

## 1. The engine in one picture

Value in this system is a set of **postings between accounts**. There is no
balance field that anybody writes directly.

```
   FAUCETS                 THE LEDGER                    MEMBERS
   sys:gratitude-pool  ─┐                            ┌─ mem:<user id>
   sys:cycle-pool      ─┤                            │
   sys:voice-mint      ─┼──▶  token_ledger  ────────▶┤   (materialised on
   sys:mint            ─┤     append-only            │    first touch)
   sys:library-mint    ─┘     idempotency_key        └─
                                   │
                                   │ SUM()
                                   ▼
                             token_balances
                          a CACHE, not the truth
```

Four things follow from that shape, and they are the whole design:

1. **The ledger is the record.** `token_balances` is a cache of
   `SUM(token_ledger)`. If they disagree, the ledger is right and the cache is
   broken.
2. **A faucet's negative balance IS the issued supply.** The reconciliation panel
   reads it that way rather than as a fault. The invariant is that every token
   sums to **zero** across all accounts including its faucet.
3. **Every posting carries an idempotency key**, and the key includes the token
   slug, so one occurrence paying two tokens writes two rows instead of one
   collision.
4. **A slug is forever.** Ledger rows key on it, so a rename would silently
   re-point history. `slugFreezeRefusal` enforces this in code, because this
   database has no foreign keys to do it (see §8).

`postTransfer` in `server/lib/ledger.ts` is the single door every posting goes
through. It takes MINOR units. That fact is the source of the most expensive
subtlety in this system; see §7.

### What triggers a posting

| Trigger | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A steward confirms a quest | consent route, then `mintForConfirmedClaim` | Gratitude is posted by the route; the rule engine deliberately SKIPS the gratitude slug so one piece of work cannot pay twice |
| A moon closes | `runSettlement` | Pays seat holders per `mint_rules` on `role.cycle` |
| A member thanks another | `give()` | Spends the member's cycle allowance |
| An admin mints by hand | admin mint | Capped per cycle, refused when the admin is the recipient |
| A member spends | the sinks in `server/lib/spending.ts` | |
| A member leaves | `sweepBalances` in `server/lib/exit.ts` | Moves the remaining balance to `sys:exit-settlement` |
| A claim confirms on Base | the Hypha webhook receiver | Reconciles a one-way bridge; see §6 |

## 2. The state of the live village, measured

| | |
|---|---|
| `token_ledger` | **0 entries** |
| `token_balances` | **0 rows** |
| `gratitude_log` | **0 rows** |
| `users` | 5 (3 of them examples) |
| `quest_claims` | 1, status `claimed`, never confirmed |
| migrations applied | 114 |
| economy epoch | stamped `2026-09-01T09:33:03.797Z` |

**No token has ever moved in this system.** It is the single most useful fact in
this document. Every decision below is still cheap, and nobody should describe
any part of this economy as proven in production. It is proven by tests, by
deliberate exercise (§9), and by one village that has not yet spent anything.

The epoch matters because of what stamped it. For one release `economyEpoch` both
read the epoch and created it, and its only caller was the mint, so the first
confirmed quest in a village's life wrote the epoch and was then ruled out by it,
losing its own payout by about twenty milliseconds. Fixed: `startEconomyEpoch` is
now called at boot. Amora's epoch carries a boot timestamp and its ledger is
empty, which proves it was stamped by the boot and not by a lost quest. **Amora
never lost a payout, because Amora has never confirmed a quest.**

---

## 3. The seven tokens

Two of the nine rows in the live `tokens` table are examples (`is_example = 1`).
The seven real ones:

| Slug | Name | Kind | Governed by | Decimals | Sendable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gratitude` | Gratitude | recognition | the village | 0 | no |
| `credits` | Village Credits | credit | the village | 0 | **yes** |
| `village-voice` | Village Voice | voice | the village | **3** | no |
| `library-credit` | Library Credit | credit | the village | 0 | no |
| `stay-credit` | Stay Credits | credit | the village | 0 | no |
| `equity` | the village's own name | equity | Hypha, on Base | 0 | no |
| `voice` | Voice | voice | Hypha, on Base | 0 | no |

`governance` splits the table in two and is the most important column in it.
`platform` means this software mints it and this software is the record. `hypha`
means the real thing lives on Base and the row here is a **mirror**: a number
this village read from a chain it does not control. Never write a hypha token as
though minting it here creates anything.

The equity row is the one place a village's own name is correct. On Amora it
reads `Amora`, because migration `0124` sets the neutral name only where the
current name is not the village's own. A village that never chose one gets
`Village Equity`.

`credits` is the only token a member can send to another member.

---

## 4. Where tokens come from

Five faucets, all present on production: `sys:gratitude-pool`, `sys:cycle-pool`,
`sys:voice-mint`, `sys:mint`, `sys:library-mint`.

Live `mint_rules` on Amora:

| Trigger | Token | Amount | Ceiling | Recipient | On |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `quest.completed` | `credits` | 25 | 250 | claimant | yes |
| `quest.completed` | `village-voice` | 10 | 100 | claimant | yes |
| `role.cycle` | `credits` | 25 | 250 | holder | yes |
| `role.cycle` | `village-voice` | 50 | 200 | holder | yes |
| `role.cycle` | `gratitude` | 20 | 100 | holder | **no** |

That last row is off by Rye's ruling of 2026-08-30, shipped as `0125`. It is
shipped off rather than deleted because **there is no route that CREATES a mint
rule**: the admin route edits an existing row, so a deleted rule is a payout the
village could never make again.

---

## 5. The gratitude cycle

Gratitude is recognition and is not meant to accumulate. Every member receives an
allowance at the start of each lunar cycle to give away, and what they do not
give expires when the cycle closes.

**The allowance is never stored.** It is computed from the ledger each time it is
asked. A stored allowance is a number that can disagree with the ledger, and the
ledger is the record.

Every gratitude write holds one lock, so a member cannot race themselves into
spending the same allowance twice. That guard is real and proven (§9). It is also
the source of the most serious defect in this engine today (§10.1).

---

## 6. Village Voice and the one-way bridge

Village Voice is the governance weight the village mints for itself. It is the
only platform token with decimals, so it stores thousandths: a rule that pays 10
posts 10000.

A member with enough of it can **claim**, which is the bridge to Base. The claim
debits the private balance at request time and the on-chain confirmation
reconciles it. The threshold is a game variable, not a constant.

The bridge is one way by design. Rye, 2026-08-31: stage 1 is the one-way bridge,
stage 2 is full Hypha integration, stage 3 is the village's own game minting
directly to Base. **What exists today is stage 1.**

---

## 7. Units and decimals, and the thing to know before changing them

`token_ledger.amount` stores MINOR units, as a `bigint` since `0126`. A token's
`decimals` column says how many. `toLedgerUnits()` and `fromLedgerUnits()`
convert.

Today six of the seven tokens have `decimals = 0` and Village Voice has 3.

**Setting every token to 4 decimals is not a migration. It is a sweep of the code
that posts to the ledger.** This is the least obvious thing in this document and
the most expensive to get wrong.

Of `postTransfer`'s 44 callers, **5 convert and 39 hand it a human number**. Those
39 are not wrong today, because at `decimals = 0` a human number and a minor unit
are the same number. `give()` is the plainest case: it posts `amount` straight
through. Set Gratitude to 4 decimals without touching that line and every give
posts **0.0020**.

The obvious repair is also wrong. Converting inside `postTransfer` would break
`sweepBalances`, which reads balances that are ALREADY minor units and posts them
unchanged, so a departing member's settlement would be multiplied by ten
thousand. **The units question has to be answered per caller**, with a test per
path.

`mint_rules.amount` is `decimal(18,4)` while the tokens it pays are `decimals 0`,
so a founder can save a rule for an amount the registry then rounds away.

---

## 8. What is enforced, and what is only convention

**Enforced by code or by a gate:**

- Every token sums to zero across all accounts. `checkLedgerInvariants` checks
  it, and the e2e suite asserts it.
- A posting is idempotent on `idempotency_key`, which carries the token slug.
- A token slug never changes once set (`slugFreezeRefusal`).
- Migrations only expand (`scripts/check-migration-compat.mjs`), so the previous
  release can still read a database the newest one migrated.
- `docs/TOKENS.md` matches the code (`scripts/check-token-doc.mjs`).

**Convention only, and worth knowing:**

- **The database has ZERO foreign keys across 153 tables**, and one check
  constraint. Every relational invariant here lives in application code. That is
  why the slug freeze had to be a code refusal.
- The 39 unconverted `postTransfer` callers in §7.
- A rule can be saved for an amount smaller than its token's resolution. The
  engine reports it as `unpayable` rather than paying zero silently, which is
  right, but nothing stops the rule being saved.
- Faucets may go negative, and member accounts may too, by ruling. Nothing in the
  schema distinguishes an intended negative from a bug.

---

## 9. What has actually been proven

An audit drove real value through a scratch database and through the built
production server. This is the part that earns trust:

- **Conservation never broke.** Not through a gratitude give, a confirmed quest,
  a settlement, a sink spend, an exit sweep, a hand mint, a deliberate
  nine-quadrillion posting, or three kinds of concurrent race.
- **Idempotency is real, not asserted.** The same claim confirmed four times at
  once paid exactly once. Five settlement runs on one cycle wrote exactly eight
  rows per token.
- **The allowance cannot be overspent by a member racing themselves.** Sixty
  simultaneous gives of 5 against an allowance of 100 spent exactly 100, over
  three runs.

That is a strong keystone and it is genuinely built. What follows is what sits on
top of it.

---

## 10. Known defects, with their measurements

### 10.1 Two members thanking at the same moment deadlock

`writeGratitudeRow` runs at SERIALIZABLE, taking gap locks over the whole
`gratitude_log` cycle range, which every giver in the village shares. **The lock
that correctly stops one member racing themselves is what makes the village fail
against each other.**

Measured through the built server over HTTP: 2 concurrent givers, 1 fails; 4, two
fail; 8, six fail; **12, ten fail**, one of them an uncaught throw rather than a
handled 400. The failure body carries raw driver text.

### 10.2 A member can be charged for a credit that was never delivered

`give()` commits the note, which SPENDS the allowance, and posts the ledger
credit afterwards, outside the lock. Under contention that post throws. Measured:
**20 to 30 of every 100 charged units never delivered**, across three runs.

`checkLedgerInvariants` cannot see it, because nothing was created out of
balance; nothing was created at all. So the founder's reconciliation panel reports
a clean economy over a real loss, and there is no repair sweep.

### 10.3 The wallet is wrong by a factor of a thousand

`fromLedgerUnits` has exactly **one** non-test caller. A member holding 10 Village
Voice reads **10** on their profile chip and **10000** on their wallet. The wallet
is the one they will believe.

This must be fixed BEFORE the 4-decimals sweep. Today one token is wrong;
afterwards every token is wrong by 10,000x on every surface that does not divide.

### 10.4 `reverse()` takes its amount from the caller

It checks only that some row with the original key exists. An audit reversed a
25-credit posting into a **1,000,000-credit payment** to the same member, and
every invariant stayed green. It should derive from the original ledger row and
refuse any caller value that disagrees.

### 10.5 `postTransfer` has no deadlock retry

`postTransferPair` carries a three-attempt retry; `postTransfer` does not.

**None of these has ever hurt anyone, because production has zero ledger rows.
All of them land on the first day more than one person uses the thing.**

---

## 11. Open decisions

1. **Decimals. RULED 2026-09-04: Village Credits gets 2 decimals. The 4-across-
   the-board sweep is cancelled.** The work belongs to the economics engine
   session; nobody else changes a token's scale.

   Rye's ruling, in his own shape: *if a bunch of work is already done to move
   them all to 4 decimals and we're already nearly there, then finish the work.
   If not, all I want is that currency-like tokens (the village credits) need to
   have 2 decimals.*

   **None of that work was done**, which is what settles it. Measured
   2026-09-04: zero migrations change any token's `decimals`, `VOICE_DECIMALS` is
   still 3, and no token has moved. The only decimals-adjacent things that landed
   were `0126` widening `token_ledger.amount` to `bigint`, which was preparation,
   and the wallet and send-card fixes, which were bugs caused by Village Voice's
   EXISTING 3 decimals rather than sweep work.

   So the scope is one token: `credits`, from 0 to 2, because two decimals is
   what money looks like everywhere else and a village currently cannot price
   anything at 12.50. `library-credit` and `stay-credit` are vouchers where a
   whole unit may be the honest shape and are NOT covered by this ruling; if the
   economics session thinks they should move, that is a question to put back.
   `village-voice` stays at 3: it is governance weight rather than currency, and
   its scale exists so a rule minting 0.1 voice does not post zero.

   **It is still not a column change.** The per-caller units problem in §7
   applies to every path that posts `credits`: `postTransfer` takes minor units,
   most of its callers hand it a human number, and they are correct today only
   because `credits` sits at 0 where the two are the same number.

2. **Whether an audit event is a guarantee.** 62 `void recordEvent` calls post the
   audit trail without awaiting it, so a member who acts and immediately opens the
   audit feed can miss their own action. Fine as best effort, wrong if the feed is
   a control.
3. **What proves this engine.** Nothing short of one real cycle in a real village,
   with several members acting at once, separates "proven by its tests" from
   "proven". See `PLAN_TO_A.md`.
